info.desc: "Ten" is the debut album by the Pearl Jam, released on August 27, 1991 through Epic Records. Following the disbanding of bassist Jeff Ament and guitarist Stone Gossard's previous group Mother Love Bone, the two recruited vocalist Eddie Vedder, guitarist Mike McCready, and drummer Dave Krusen to form Pearl Jam in 1990. Most of the songs began as instrumental jams, to which Vedder added lyrics about topics such as depression, homelessness, and abuse. "Ten" was not an immediate success, but by late 1992 it had reached number two on the Billboard 200 chart. The album produced three hit singles: "Alive", .

podcast.body: The album *Ten* was released shortly after 1989, following the first album by Nirvana and Alice in Chains, marking a period when grunge was becoming widely known. Pearl Jam is noted for incorporating a very classic rock version within the grunge sound. "salía el 10 de Pell Yam."

podcast.body: "Ten" was Pearl Jam's debut album, released on August 8, 1991. It was identified as the first of three crucial albums, alongside Soundgarden's "Bad Motor Finger" and Nirvana's "Nevermind," that collectively ignited the grunge explosion in the US Pacific Northwest. "Pearl Jam was the first to break out with a ten album back at the 8th of August."

podcast.body: A 180g reissue of the album _10_ was released in 2009 as part of a box set. This version is a remaster, meaning that producers and engineers went back to the original master tapes to create a new recording using the latest available technologies, aiming for enhanced sound quality. "This is from a 180g reissue of Pearl Jam's 10 album released as part of a box set in 2009."

podcast.body: After releasing clips for the first four singles from their debut album *Ten*, Pearl Jam notably refused to produce any more music videos for approximately six years. However, one additional black and white video for the song "Oceans" from *Ten* was released, but only outside the US. "There would be one more video from Pearl Jam's 10 album, and the song was Oceans, which was a black and white film of the band in Hawaii."

podcast.body: Pearl Jam released their debut record on August 28, 1991, the same day Nirvana released "Smells Like Teen Spirit." This release occurred just as the first Lollapalooza tour was wrapping up. "And it was also on that day that a new group called Pearl Jam put out their debut record."

podcast.body: Pearl Jam's debut album, "Ten," showcased an evolution towards a more outward-facing and "rabid" perspective, influenced by Rage Against the Machine's approach to confronting the world and its systems. This marked a significant shift from the purely introspective themes typically associated with Grunge music. "Tú escuchas el primer álbum de Perlham y escuchas el ten, y ves ahí una evolución más rabiosa hacia el mundo y el sistema, yo creo que gracias a cómo rechagan semacín había un poco abierto los ojos a la generación X."

podcast.body: Pearl Jam's debut album, released in the last week of August 1991. It initially made little impact but eventually became double platinum by late summer 1992, driven by the singles "Alive," "Evenflow," and "Jeremy." The album spent nearly two years climbing the charts, peaked at number two, sold six million copies, and is now certified for 13 million US sales. "Pearl Jam's debut album, Ten, didn't make much of a ripple."

podcast.body: Released on August 27, 1991, "Ten" was Pearl Jam's debut album from the Pacific Northwest. Initially overlooked, its sales grew through relentless touring and the frontman's dedication, eventually selling 11 million copies in the US and an estimated 20 million globally. This album became the first of the "holy trinity of grunge albums," marking a pivotal moment in the genre's history. "It sold 11 million copies in the US alone."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Stone Gossard gave a cassette of instrumental demos to his friend Jack Irons (who would later drum for both Pearl Jam and the Red Hot Chili Peppers). Irons passed it to a San Diego surfer and bartender who sang for a band called Bad Radio: Eddie Vedder. Eddie wrote and recorded a three-part mini-opera called "Mama-San" (comprising "Alive," "Once," and "Footsteps") over Stone's demo, using his old Tascam 4-track recorder — but the only blank tape he had was a copy of Merle Haggard's *Greatest Hits*. He taped his audition material over Merle's music and sent it to Seattle. That tape got him the gig. "The entire 12 and a half minutes of audio on this cassette was taped over a pre-recorded copy of Merle Haggard's greatest hits."
